reference: Metadata contracts use Bash's type/help builtins plus the documented timeout help and version text. Timeout operation behavior is intentionally deferred: this task forbids invoking this process-control loadable, so no operational result is claimed as parity.
coverage: Bash reports timeout as a builtin through type -t.
Bash help exposes the documented timeout synopsis, options, and status mapping.
Deferred GNU coreutils comparisons cover child status and lookup, expiration signals, duration parsing, escalation, preserve-status, SIGCHLD handling, and foreground process groups.
exclusions: No timeout operation is invoked in this suite. Operational cases require a future disposable Linux VM or reviewed private process mock with fixture-only children; none of those cases is a pass here.
Interactive --foreground behavior needs a private PTY and supervised process tree, which the fixture runner does not provide.

cases.purpose: Bash metadata contract: type -t identifies the installed timeout loadable as a builtin.
Bash help contract: expose the timeout synopsis, options, and exit-status documentation without starting a child.
cases.stdout:
timeout: timeout [--help|--version] [--preserve-status] [--foreground] [-v|--verbose] [-s SIG] [-k DUR] DURATION CMD [ARG...]
    Run a command with a time limit.
    
        timeout [--help|--version] [--preserve-status] [--foreground] [-v|--verbose]
                    [-s SIG] [-k DUR] DURATION CMD [ARG...]
    
        --help              show this help
        --version           show version
        -s SIG              initial signal (name, RTMIN[+N], RTMAX[-N], or number; default TERM)
        -k DUR              send SIGKILL if still alive DUR after the initial signal
        --preserve-status   return CMD's actual exit status even on timeout
        -v, --verbose       diagnose to stderr any signal sent upon timeout
                            (format: "timeout: sending signal NAME to command 'CMD'")
        DURATION            <number>[s|m|h|d]  (default seconds; 0 disables the timeout)
    
    Exit 124 on timeout, 125 on internal error, 126 if CMD found but
    not executable, 127 if not found, 128+N if killed by signal N,
    otherwise CMD's own exit status.  With --preserve-status, returns
    CMD's exit status (128+N) instead of 124 when timeout occurs.

cases.purpose: Verify ordinary child output and statuses 0 and 7, plus command-not-found 127 and non-executable-command 126.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM or reviewed private process mock with a fixture-only working directory, PATH, and executable/non-executable child files. Compare the timeout builtin and GNU coreutils timeout on the same cases; never point command lookup outside that fixture.

cases.purpose: Verify expiration sends the default TERM to a bounded child and returns 124 while leaving the parent shell usable.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with a private process namespace and a controlled fixture child that traps TERM and records receipt only in the private fixture directory. Compare status and child effects with GNU coreutils timeout; do not signal any process outside the fixture.

cases.purpose: Verify -s USR1 delivery and --verbose's signal diagnostic for a child that handles USR1 and exits on receipt.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with a private process namespace with a fixture child and private process group. Compare the observed signal, timeout status, and verbose stderr with GNU coreutils timeout; do not target external PIDs.

cases.purpose: Verify -k escalation after an ignored initial signal, including the exact monitor/child exit status and private group effects observed with GNU timeout.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with a private PID namespace, a fixture child that ignores TERM, a reviewed bounded cleanup supervisor and GNU timeout. Measure whether SIGKILL reaches the monitor as well as the child; GNU may return 137 rather than 124. Compare observed statuses and signals exactly; never signal host processes.

cases.purpose: Verify --preserve-status returns the child's resulting exit status after timeout instead of the default 124.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with a private process namespace and a private child that handles TERM and exits with a fixed nonzero status. Compare default and --preserve-status results against GNU coreutils timeout; all child effects must remain in the fixture.

cases.purpose: Verify zero disables the deadline, fractional seconds and s/m/h/d suffixes parse, and malformed or negative durations fail before child side effects.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed private process mock with short, bounded fixture children and a marker inside the fixture directory. Compare accepted/rejected duration cases, statuses, and marker state with GNU coreutils timeout; do not run long-duration waits.

cases.purpose: Verify a background job that exits while timeout waits is reaped by Bash, a CHLD trap remains observable, and timeout still waits for its own child.
cases.reason: Requires a future disposable Linux VM with a private PID namespace, a shell fixture with private background children, and bounded waits. Compare job state, trap observation, elapsed ordering, and final status with a documented GNU/Bash reference; inspect only fixture PIDs.

cases.purpose: Verify default process-group isolation and --foreground terminal signal behavior, including the effect on a child process tree.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable Linux VM with a private PTY/terminal driver and a supervised fixture process tree. Compare process-group membership and signal forwarding with GNU coreutils timeout, and assert all processes belong to the fixture namespace.
